texts.preamble: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Dev Raj on 30 January, 2017 IN THE COURT OF SH. ASHU GARG, Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - II (New Delhi), Patiala House Courts, New Delhi CC No. 33/11 Unique Case ID No. 02403R0013152011
texts.facts: Accused JUDGMENT: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. The accused Dev Raj is stated to be the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s. Aggarwal Sweets Corner, from where the food article, that is, 'Besan ke laddu' was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 01.11.2010, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) Virender Singh and Field Assistant (FA) S. N. Jindal under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. Ajay Kumar reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. Aggarwal Sweets Corner at B-6/114, Sector-8, Rohini, Delhi-110085, where the accused was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored/exposed for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Besan ke laddu from the vendor, to which he agreed. The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 24.11.2010, the PA found the sample to be adulterated on the ground that it contained added vegetable oil which was not declared as an ingredient. Upon receipt of Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Dev Raj on 30 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65795867/ 1 report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 09.02.2011 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a), (b), (c) and (m) of PFA Act as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 09.02.2011. The accused appeared but chose not to file any application under section 13(2) of PFA Act thereby exercising his right to get the second counterpart of the sample analysed from Central Food Laboratory (CFL). 4. On the basis of PA report, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed against the accused on 20.07.2011 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act, being violation of section 2(ia)(a), (b), (c) and (m) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. At the trial, prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 Sh. Ajay Kumar (SDM/LHA), PW-2 FI Virender Singh and PW-3 FA S. N. Jindal were examined who all were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 01.11.2010 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 1500 gms of Besan ke laddu from an open tray, breaking the same into smallest possible pieces using a clean and dry spoon, mixing/homogenizing it using the same spoon, dividing it in three parts and putting in clean and dry bottles, adding formalin (40 drops each) as preservative, fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice in Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B (on which the vendor disclosed the ingredients of the commodity) and Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C. Raid report Ex. PW-1/D was also prepared at the spot and statement of accused Ex. PW-1/E was recorded. On the next day, one counterpart of the sample with Memo as per Form-VII was deposited with PA vide PA Receipt Ex. PW-2/A and the other two counterparts with memos were deposited with LHA vide receipt Ex. PW-1/F. PA report Ex. PW-1/G was received upon which investigation was carried out by PW-2. He sent letter Ex. PW-2/B to VAT Office to ascertain the constitution of the business concern. After completion of investigation, sanction Ex. PW-1/H was taken from the Director PFA and the complaint Ex. PW-1/I was filed in the court. A copy of PA report with intimation letter Ex. PW-1/J was sent to the accused through registered post vide receipt Ex. PW-1/K. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that the some vanaspati was lying in the tray in which laddus had been broken. They could not tell if there was any standard of 'extracted fat' in PFA Act or not. 6. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 26.03.2014 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Though he admitted the proceedings dated 01.11.2010, yet he claimed that no public person was requested to join the proceedings. He denied receiving the PA report. He questioned the PA report by claiming that some vegetable oil is put on the tray by the workers/karigars when they prepare the laddus so that they do not stick to the tray. He however chose not to lead evidence in defence. Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Dev Raj on 30 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65795867/ 2 7.
texts.arguments: It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, on the ground that the accused has not been able to rebut the findings in the PA report dated 24.11.2010. It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony. 8. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel has submitted that the sample on question is a proprietary food for which there are no standards prescribed under the PFA Act or Rules. It is submitted that no standards are there for 'extracted fat' which was analysed by the PA. It is then argued that as per Rule 43(5) of PFA Rules, a seller of sweets is not required to declare the ingredients and thus, there is no violation of rules. It is maintained that vegetable oil is allowed to be used on the tray of such food articles, as "good manufacturing practice" so that they may not stick to it, and such vegetable oil might have been detected by the PA. Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature, substance or quality which it purported or represented to be. Under section 2(ia)(b) of PFA Act, it has to be established that the food article contained any substance affecting injuriously the nature, substance or quality thereof. Section 2(ia)(c) of PFA Act requires to be established that any inferior or cheaper substance has been substituted, wholly or in part, for the article so as to affect injuriously the nature, substance or quality thereof.
